# aeneid-072 (X.1–95) — drafter's notes

59 units; `make_units.py` runs clean (no LINE COUNT / TOO LONG / NEWLINE / ENDING / NOTE LENGTH warnings, plus an extra
check that “ ” [ ] counts match between t and l, and “ ” between t and i). `t` comes only from `A.cut`; no `sc`. Notes run
41–127 words (longest: the 1–4 unit). Longest units are four lines (1–4, 44–47, 55–58). Paragraphs: 1, 16 (both `p: true`;
each note opens "A new paragraph in Greenough."). Book X opens here; the first note says so.

Title `Concilium deorum`; part "The Council of the Gods (X.1–95)".

## Speech marks

- Jupiter: “ 6 (`“Caelicolae`) … ” 15 (`foedus.”`), units 6–7 and 15.
- Venus: “ 18 (`“O pater`) … ” 62 (`Teucris.”`), units 18 and 60b–62.
- Juno: “ 63 mid-line (`“Quid me`) … ” 95 (`iactas.”`), units 63b–64 and 94b–95. Her introduction (`Tum regia Iuno / acta
  furore gravi:`, 62b–63a) is its own unit.
3 “ / 3 ” in each of t, l, i.

## Line 62 / 62b

Cut as instructed: (62, 'Teucris.”') finds the first 62, then (63, 'gravi:') takes `Tum regia Iuno\nacta furore gravi:`
(ln 62, label 62b; not a paragraph start). Its note says Greenough prints a half-line 62b, two hemistichs counted as one
line 62. Its l has the same single break.

## Bracketed lines

- 20–21 `[Cernis … feratur]` `[per medios … secundo]`: in the 20–22a unit (`… Marte ruat?`), kept, translated (l bracketed as
  t; i normal); note says Greenough brackets them as doubtful and that the question cannot stand without them.
- 27 `[nascentis Troiae nec non exercitus alter;]`: the unit is 26b–27 (`Muris iterum imminet hostis / [… alter;]`), ending
  at `alter;]`; noted likewise.

## Misprint calls (rule 5b; t as printed, l/i corrected, note opens "The print has X, a misprint for Y, corrected here.")

1. **10.20 `Rutulli`** for `Rutuli` — unit 20–22a. (That note opens with the misprint sentence and then the bracket remark.)
2. **10.36 `repetem`** for `repetam` (deliberative subjunctive) — unit 36–38.
No others found. Checked and not called: capital `O` twice at 18 (an old printing habit for the interjection, not an
error); `Fortuna` capitalised at 49 (personification); punctuation at 20–21 (no commas inside the brackets — unusual but
not wrong); 89 `conamur, nos, an` (commas where others print question marks — an editorial choice); all capitals after
stops regular. Kept and explained as Greenough's spellings: `moerorum` 24, `divom` 2/65, `volnera` 29, `volgare` 64,
`inpulsus` 68, `adspectat` 4, `exscidia` 46, `adsurgis`/`inrita` 95, `-is` accusatives (`omnis` 3, `furentis` 37,
`manis` 39, `gentis` 71, `inanis` 82).

## Latin Library variants

- 24 `fossas` / `fossae`: **noted** (changes the construction: Rutulians flood the trenches vs the trenches overflow).
- 83 `tu` / `et`: **noted** briefly (loses the `tu potes… tu potes` anaphora that carries the rhetoric).
- 49 `quamcumque` / `quacumque`: not noted ("whatever way" acc. vs "by whatever way" abl. — same sense).
- 20 `Rutulli`/`Rutuli`, 36 `repetem`/`repetam`: these confirm the misprints.
- Orthography/morphology, ignored in n: `divom`/`diuum` 2, 65; `adspectat`/`aspectat` 4; `Alpes`/`Alpis` 13; `moerorum`/
  `murorum` 24; `volnera` 29; `classes`/`classis` 36; `exscidia`/`excidia` 46; `ignes`/`ignis` 56; `volgare` 64;
  `inpulsus` 68.

## Other things for the reviewer

- Half-line 17 `pauca refert:` noted as unfinished (scanner flags 17 UNRESOLVED for that reason). 62 and 62b each scan
  as hemistichs only (flagged UNRESOLVED): need half-line / split-line scan-fixes entries.
- 20 flagged UNRESOLVED, presumably because of `Rutulli` (double l makes `-tul-` long); with `Rutuli`: cēr-nĭs ŭt | īn-
  sūl | tēnt Rŭ-tŭ | lī Tūr | nūs-quĕ fĕ | rā-tur. The scan-fix should use the corrected reading.
- 89 (COSTLY): cō-nā | mūr nōs | ān mĭ-sĕ | rōs quī | Trō-ăs Ă | chī-vis — `Troas` two syllables, `qui` long, no hiatus.
- 73 `Ubi hic`: elision ub(i) hic; ē-gĭt ŭ | b(i) hīc Iū | nō dē | mīs-să-vĕ | nū-bĭ-bŭs | Ī-ris. Worth a hand check.
- 18 `O pater, O hominum`: the interjection O does not elide (hiatus), stated in the note.
- 44 `nulla est`: listed as elision `null(a) est` (could be prodelision `nulla 'st`).
- Greek eu: `Teucris` 8, 44, 62; `Teucros` 22, 28; `Teucri` 58. Ae-: `Aeneas` 25,
  48, 85; `Aenean` 65, 81; `Aeolia` 38; `Aetolis` 28. Consonantal i after prefix: `coniunx` 44, `obiecit` 90.
- Interpretations hedged/chosen: 3 `sententia versa retro` — noted that the poem shows no earlier ban; 40 `movet`'s subject
  taken as Juno (Allecto possible); 58 `exhausta (esse)` as third infinitive; 71 `agitare` governing both `fidem` and
  `gentis`; 84 `contra` adverbial; 87 `urbem` as the Latin state.

## Attributions (please check)

- From memory, unchecked: Iliad 4 and 8 opening councils (8 = Zeus forbids the gods to fight); Iliad 5 (Diomedes wounds
  Aphrodite as she carries Aeneas off; Aeneas then hidden in a cloud — by Apollo in Homer, which the note sidesteps);
  Ennius as source of the `divom pater atque hominum rex` formula and of `quianam`; Book III Anchises on Cassandra;
  Book VII `flectere si nequeo superos, Acheronta movebo` (VII.312); Book VII Trojan envoys with olive branches;
  Book IX ships turned to nymphs by the Mother of the Gods; Book VIII envoy to Diomedes; Pilumnus as Turnus's ancestor
  (also IX.4), Venilia a nymph; `fuimus Troes` (II.325).
